profile.name: Mozaddid Ul Hoque Babar
profile.title: Machine Learning Researcher & Software Engineer
profile.headline: Machine Learning • NLP & Data Mining (Prospective PhD) • Biomedical Signal Processing
profile.bio: Machine learning researcher with a background in biomedical signal processing, applying feature engineering and predictive modeling to healthcare diagnostics (EEG-based depression detection, multi-class diabetes prediction). Currently an Associate Software Engineer building production systems with Next.js, Node, and React. Applying to doctoral programs for Fall 2027 to pursue research in Natural Language Processing and Data Mining.
aboutText: My research background began in biomedical signal processing at the HSTU Research Lab, where I worked on feature extraction and machine learning pipelines for EEG and ECG data, including correlation-based feature selection for major depressive disorder detection.

This work led to three publications applying machine learning to healthcare diagnostics — spanning EEG-based depression prediction and multi-class diabetes mellitus classification using filtered clinical data.

Alongside research, I have 2+ years of professional software engineering experience (Next.js, Node, Express, React), which I see as a strength for NLP and data mining research: the ability to build, scale, and deploy the systems that research prototypes need to become usable tools.
I am now applying to doctoral programs for Fall 2027 to extend my background in structured feature engineering and pattern discovery toward Natural Language Processing and Data Mining.

publications.title: Optimal Feature Identification and Major Depressive Disorder Prediction through Correlation-Based Machine Learning Approach
publications.authors: MUH Babar, J Ferdouse, A Bhuyain, M Sohrawordi, E Ali
publications.venue: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Information and …, 2024
publications.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a mental health disorder characterized by continuous feelings of sadness, diminished interest in activities, and a range of physical and emotional symptoms that profoundly affect a person’s daily life and functioning. Early detection of MDD is crucial for improved treatment outcomes. The detection of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) relies on extracting several features from raw EEG signals. This study presents a machine learning-based approach to identify MDD using minimal EEG signal features, employing a correlation analysis with various correlation coefficient values. The proposed method achieved an impressive accuracy of 84% with SVM, showing 91.5% sensitivity, 75.5% specificity, and 85.7% f1-score with best correlation coefficient value. To evaluate performance, 5-fold cross-validation with inter-subject variability is utilized. The study extracts several feature sets …

publications.title: An efficient feature optimization approach with machine learning for detection of major depressive disorder using EEG signal
publications.authors: AR Bhuyain, J Ferdouse, MUH Babar, M Sohrawordi, MR Islam, E Ali
publications.venue: 2023 26th International conference on computer and information technology …, 2023
publications.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a mental health condition marked by persistent feelings of sadness, diminished interest in once-enjoyable activities, and an array of physical and emotional symptoms that profoundly disrupt an individual's daily life and functioning. In this circumstance, detecting major depressive disorder in the early phase is required. Identifying Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) involves the extraction of multiple features from unprocessed EEG signals. This study proposed a machine learning approach to identify minimum possible features as 14 significant features by removing highly correlated features and applying a Genetic algorithm with several combinations of maximum features. The proposed method obtained an accuracy of 84.1% in AdaBoost, 80.1% in DecissionTree, 85.5% in RandomForest, 84.9% Gradient Boosting, 84.9% in XG Boosting.
